groups.meaning: a cell belongs to a group by the calendar flags of its target day T as recorded in the 1363 walk file (targets[T].types, from the day table the candidate reads at the target day, and targets[T].pressure). The flag groups overlap: a day with two flags is in both. Every group is read on its own cells, all five horizons pooled
groups.quarter_end_flag: targets[T].types contains quarter_end (the calendar flag, for reference)
groups.quarter_end_group_1533: cells whose pressure-day type is quarter_end_turn or year_end, resampled by quarter-end event: the group of #1533, the reproduction check and the reference
groups.no_flag: targets[T].types == ['ordinary'] and targets[T].pressure == 'ordinary': no calendar flag and no pressure-day type
groups.overlap: for each flag group the page gives the share of its target days that also carry another of the listed flags, and the share of its cells that fall in the quarter-end group of #1533

statistic.same_as: docs/research/qe-diagnosis-1533 item_2b_width_or_shape, by scripts/qe_diagnosis_1533.py shape_ratios: for the group's cells with q95 > q05 on the raw (pre-cap) quantiles, z = (y - q50)/(q95 - q05); the law's z_tau = mean over the cells of (q_tau - q50)/(q95 - q05); the realised distance r_tau = (quantile tau of z) - (median of z); ratio_tau = r_tau / law_tau. median_z is the location shift in units of the forecast's 90% span
statistic.tails: one at a time: lower q05 (ratio_0.05), upper q95 (ratio_0.95). Also q01 and q99 for a group with at least 500 cells (five expected misses at the 1% level); below that they are shown as 'too few' with no ratio
statistic.the_middle: ratio_0.25 and ratio_0.75 are reported beside, as in #1533, and are not used by the reading
statistic.interval: 90% percentile interval from the stationary bootstrap of the group's target days in date order (mean block 10, 1000 resamples, seed 1547; every cell of a drawn target day comes with it); the quarter-end group of #1533 by whole events (1000 resamples, seed 1547). The interval of each ratio, of the median shift, of the difference ratio_0.95 - ratio_0.05 and, where reported, ratio_0.01 - ratio_0.05 and ratio_0.99 - ratio_0.95, all from the same resamples
statistic.paired: beside the ratios, for each group the mean paired grid CRPS and upper-tail twCRPS difference of the candidate minus B1' and minus B2 on the same cells (negative favours the candidate), with the same interval; and the strict miss rates below q05 and above q95 against the nominal 0.05, with the same interval
statistic.splits: by regime (point values; a split with fewer than 30 usable cells is shown as 'too few'), by lead, and by pressure-day type of the target (point values), for every group

reading_rule.meaning: How a group's tail is called a width, a shape or a location problem. Her ruling asked for 'the same rule declared in metadata/qe_diagnosis_1533.json'. That declaration states the rule in words: 'a pure width problem shows one ratio common to all levels (and to both sides); a shape problem shows ratios that grow towards the tails or differ by side', and the shift is the median of z. It does not say what counts as 'common' or 'differ'. The operational reading below is this study's own and is marked as a question for Eleonora in the pull request. It is applied mechanically to the development window and nothing here is chosen after a figure
reading_rule.tail_off: a tail is 'too thin' when the 90% interval of its ratio lies wholly above 1 (realised outcomes reach further from the median than the forecast law does), 'too wide' when wholly below 1, 'in line' when it contains 1
reading_rule.location: the group has a location problem when the 90% interval of median_z excludes 0
reading_rule.width: both q05 and q95 are off in the same direction and the interval of ratio_0.95 - ratio_0.05 contains 0 (one ratio common to both sides)
reading_rule.shape: the interval of ratio_0.95 - ratio_0.05 excludes 0 (the sides differ), or, where q01/q99 are reported, the interval of ratio_0.01 - ratio_0.05 or of ratio_0.99 - ratio_0.95 excludes 0 (the ratio changes with the level)
reading_rule.one_tail: exactly one of q05 and q95 is off, the other in line, and the interval of their difference contains 0: reported as 'one tail off, not separable from width'
reading_rule.labels: a group may carry location together with width or shape; 'in line' when no tail is off and the shift interval contains 0; shape takes precedence over width when both are met
reading_rule.per_tail: the page gives one line per group and tail: in line / too thin / too wide, the ratio and interval, the number of expected misses

arm_rule.meaning: Which per-tail arm the evidence supports, by rule, using only flags the candidate already reads at the target day (dom_19_23 and post_month_end_window are terms of the fit; coupon_settlement is the settlement_coupon term; quarter_end is a flag it reads). The arm is named, not built, here
arm_rule.candidates: a scale of one tail by flag, where that tail is off; a shift by flag, where the group has a location problem
arm_rule.supported_when: the development window shows it (the tail is off, or the location interval excludes 0) AND the point value is on the same side of 1 (resp. 0) in a majority of the regimes that hold at least 30 usable cells for that group; the 2026 point value on the same side is shown apart and does not decide
arm_rule.otherwise: the evidence cannot yet tell, said plainly, with the reason (interval contains 1 or 0, regimes disagree, too few cells)
arm_rule.no_values: no multiplier or shift size is chosen or fitted here; that is the second step's, after review

limits: development data on seen days, never a verdict; the 2026 days are shown apart and decide nothing
the flag groups overlap, and the ordinary group is defined by the absence of every flag; a day in two groups counts in both
the ratio is descriptive: it is inflated by any location shift the median removes imperfectly, and an interval from a few dozen target days is wide
the hit counts of #1523 are at lead 1 against a regime-expected rate fitted in sample; this study pools all five leads and uses the candidate's own nominal levels
the operational reading rule is this study's own; the pull request marks it as a question for Eleonora
